**Oakville** was a federal [electoral district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_district_(Canada) "Electoral district (Canada)") in [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario"), Canada, that was represented in the [House of Commons of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_Canada "House of Commons of Canada") from 1997 to 2025.

After the [2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Canadian_federal_electoral_redistribution "2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution"), the riding was abolished and divided into [Oakville East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville_East "Oakville East") and [Oakville West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville_West "Oakville West") for the [2025 Canadian federal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Canadian_federal_election "2025 Canadian federal election").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oakville_(federal_electoral_district)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

It was created in 1996 from parts of [Halton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halton_(federal_electoral_district) "Halton (federal electoral district)") and [Oakville—Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville%E2%80%94Milton "Oakville—Milton") ridings.

It consisted initially of the part of the Town of [Oakville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville,_Ontario "Oakville, Ontario") lying southeast of the Queen Elizabeth Way and Upper Middle Road.

In 2003, it was redefined to consist of the part of the Town of Oakville lying southeast of a line drawn from the northeastern town limit southwest along Dundas Street East, southeast along Eighth Line and southwest along Upper Middle Road to the southwestern town limit. This riding was unchanged after the [2012 electoral redistribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_federal_electoral_redistribution,_2012 "Canadian federal electoral redistribution, 2012").

The current boundaries include the neighbourhoods of Lakeshore Woods, Bronte, Hopedale, Coronation Park, Kerr Village, Old Oakville, Eastlake, Glen Abbey, College Park, Iroquois Ridge, Clearview, and Joshua Creek.

**Oakville** was a federal [electoral district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_district_(Canada) "Electoral district (Canada)") in [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario"), Canada, that was represented in the [House of Commons of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_Canada "House of Commons of Canada") from 1997 to 2025.

After the [2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Canadian_federal_electoral_redistribution "2022 Canadian federal electoral redistribution"), the riding was abolished and divided into [Oakville East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville_East "Oakville East") and [Oakville West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville_West "Oakville West") for the [2025 Canadian federal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Canadian_federal_election "2025 Canadian federal election").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oakville_(federal_electoral_district)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

It was created in 1996 from parts of [Halton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halton_(federal_electoral_district) "Halton (federal electoral district)") and [Oakville—Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville%E2%80%94Milton "Oakville—Milton") ridings.

It consisted initially of the part of the Town of [Oakville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakville,_Ontario "Oakville, Ontario") lying southeast of the Queen Elizabeth Way and Upper Middle Road.

In 2003, it was redefined to consist of the part of the Town of Oakville lying southeast of a line drawn from the northeastern town limit southwest along Dundas Street East, southeast along Eighth Line and southwest along Upper Middle Road to the southwestern town limit. This riding was unchanged after the [2012 electoral redistribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_federal_electoral_redistribution,_2012 "Canadian federal electoral redistribution, 2012").

The current boundaries include the neighbourhoods of Lakeshore Woods, Bronte, Hopedale, Coronation Park, Kerr Village, Old Oakville, Eastlake, Glen Abbey, College Park, Iroquois Ridge, Clearview, and Joshua Creek.

Global News is declaring Anita Anand, Liberal Party of Canada, re-elected in Oakville East.

![Image 10](https://d21y75miwcfqoq.cloudfront.net/70c8fc80)
Oakville East is a federal riding located in Ontario.

This new federal riding contains parts of the ridings previously known as Oakville and Oakville-North Burlington.

Voters will decide who will represent Oakville East in Ontario during the upcoming Canadian election on April 28, 2025.

Visit this page on election night for a complete breakdown of up to the minute results.

 Oakville News Staff Apr 28, 2025 9:30 PM

The local results of Canada's 2025 federal election are almost complete. Both Sima Acan and Anita Anand for the Liberals have been elected as MPs for Oakville West and Oakville East respectively.

In total, a record-breaking number of Canadians cast their vote. More than 18.2 million balltos were cast in this election.

This website will be updating live tonight as results are reported by the polling stations.

For the latest developments in the national race, go to our[Canada Votes page](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-canada-votes).

Live results from the new Oakville West and East ridings will available on this website all night long just below in this story. Up-to-the-minute updates from Oakville and across Canada are available below those graphs.

Polls are now closed in Oakville, and results are available here:

* * *

## _Live updates across Oakville:_

**_3:00 a.m.:_**This concludes Oakville News' live coverage of Canada's Election Night 2025. This story and its links will remain on the website indefinitely. Good night!

_**2:45 a.m.:**_ No additional polls have submitted results in the last hour, and final results aren't expected until at least tomorrow.

_**2:30 a.m.:**_ Around Halton, Liberal candidates have won in Burlington and Burlington North-Milton West, while Conservatives won in Wellington-Halton Hills. The new Milton East-Halton Hills South riding is still too close to call, though Conservative Parm Gill has a 0.2 per cent lead as of press time.

_**2:15 a.m.:**_ Oakville News has spoken with campaign officials for Tim Crowder and Ron Chhinzer, and neither have responded to our requests for comment. There has also been no comment from Alicia Bedford, who ran for the United Party in Oakville East.

_**2:00 a.m.:**_ Almost all polls are now reporting in Oakville, and the results are nearly final. Only one poll in Oakville West and five polls in Oakville East have yet to send in their results.

In Oakville West, with 194/195 polls reporting:

*   **Sima Acan,LIB**- 30,440 votes, 52.71 %
*   **Tim Crowder,CON**- 25,848 votes, 44.76 %
*   **Diane Downey,NDP**- 800 votes, 1.39 %
*   **Chris Kowalchuk,GRN**- 352 votes, 0.61 %
*   **JD Meaney,PPC**- 247 votes, 0.43 %
*   **Martin Gegus,IND**- 60 votes, 0.10 %

In Oakville East, with 189/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 29,904 votes, 50.71 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 26,626 votes, 45.15 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 1,653 votes, 2.80 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 341 votes, 0.58 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 320 votes, 0.54 %
*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 130 votes, 0.22 %

_**1:45 a.m.:**_ While final votes are still being certified, it is expected that **Canada will be forming its third consecutive Liberal minority government.**

_**1:35 a.m.:**_ Newly elected Prime Minister Mark Carney, addressing Canadians at his acceptance speech, says "When Canada seeks unity and kindness, Canada grows."

_**1:15 a.m.:**_ Re-elected MP Anita Anand, on her win tonight, told Oakville News that, "It's about making sure that we're able to stand out for the values that make Canada strong."

_**1:10 a.m.:**_ On her win tonight, newly elected Oakville West MP Sima Acan told Oakville News: "This is life changing. It's a step that I am taking now for public service which was always in me."

![Image 2: simaacan_2025_election](https://www.vmcdn.ca/f/files/oakville/images/politicians/simaacan_2025_election.jpg;w=960)

_**1:05 a.m.:**_ Oakville News is waiting on comment from both Tim Crowder or Ron Chhinzer tonight with the Oakville Conservatives. We expect remarks from Crowder later tonight, though Chhinzer has not responded to our requests for comment.

_**1:00 a.m.:**_ While final results won't be certified until much later on Tuesday, Oakville News has called the race for both Oakville West and Oakville East, with more than 90 per cent of polls reporting results.

In Oakville West, with 180/195 polls reporting:

*   **Sima Acan,LIB**- 26,139 votes, 52.55 %
*   **Tim Crowder,CON**- 22,299 votes, 44.83 %
*   **Diane Downey,NDP**- 715 votes, 1.44 %
*   **Chris Kowalchuk,GRN**- 313 votes, 0.63 %
*   **JD Meaney,PPC**- 225 votes, 0.45 %
*   **Martin Gegus,IND**- 54 votes, 0.11 %

In Oakville East, with 181/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 26,852 votes, 50.17 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 24,377 votes, 45.55 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 1,543 votes, 2.88 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 323 votes, 0.60 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 294 votes, 0.55 %
*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 129 votes, 0.24 %

_**12:40 p.m.:**_ Following what appears to be a loss of 17 seats nationwide, Jagmeet Singh has resigned as leader of the New Democratic Party.

_**12:30 p.m.:**_ For the Green Party, Oakville News has reached out to both local candidates.

Chris Kowalchuk, candidate for Oakville West, said, "Thanks to the voters of Oakville. I've met Sima several times and I'm sure she will represent all people of Oakville well. I look forward to working with her on issues of mutual concern."

Bruno Sousa, candidate for Oakville East, did not respond to our requests for comment.

_**12:25 a.m.:**_**OAKVILLE NEWS PROJECTS SIMA ACAN ELECTED AS MP FOR OAKVILLE WEST**

Acan is leading by eight points, with 82 per cent of the vote reporting. Acan goes to Ottawa for her first term. [The full story is available by clicking here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-sima-acan-elected-as-first-mp-for-oakville-west-10581920).

_**12:05 a.m.:**_**OAKVILLE NEWS PROJECTS ANITA ANAND ELECTED AS MP FOR OAKVILLE EAST**

Anand is leading by four and a half points, with 85 per cent of the vote reporting. Anand returns to Ottawa for a third term, having won in the former Oakville riding in 2019 and 2021.[The full](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-anita-anand-elected-mp-for-oakville-east-10581935)[story is available by clicking here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-anita-anand-elected-mp-for-oakville-east-10581935).

![Image 3: anitaanandwin1](https://www.vmcdn.ca/f/files/oakville/images/politicians/anitaanandwin1.jpg;w=960)

_**12:01 a.m.:**_ It's now midnight on Tuesday morning, April 29. Neither of Oakville's new ridings have been called yet. Just over 75 per cent of polls have reported local results. Both Liberal candidates maintain slight leads.

In Oakville West, with 145/195 polls reporting:

*   **Sima Acan,LIB**- 16,591 votes, 51.75 %
*   **Tim Crowder,CON**- 14,536 votes, 45.34 %
*   **Diane Downey,NDP**- 503 votes, 1.57 %
*   **Chris Kowalchuk,GRN**- 240 votes, 0.75 %
*   **JD Meaney,PPC**- 154 votes, 0.48 %
*   **Martin Gegus,IND**- 39 votes, 0.12 %

In Oakville East, with 165/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 20,989 votes, 49.89 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 19,130 votes, 45.48 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 1,289 votes, 3.06 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 284 votes, 0.68 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 254 votes, 0.60 %
*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 121 votes, 0.29 %

_**11:45 p.m.:**_ Oakville News has spoken with Martin Gegus, independent in Oakville West, on tonight's results:

_"I went into this campaign with the desire to leave a positive impact on our community. Running as an Independent without strong name recognition, I had no illusions of winning against my political rivals._

_I was, however, able to use my run at office to secure short term employment for several students and low income members of the Oakville community and from that standpoint, the campaign was a real success._

_I would like to extend my congratulations to the leading contenders and well as my gratitude to my fellow Oakville residents who signed my nomination papers and gave me the opportunity partake in Canada's democratic tradition. I would also like to thank my family who stood by my side and supported me during the past few weeks as I focused almost exclusive on getting the message out._

_Finally, a thank you to Oakville's voters who came out to exercise their democratic right to choose their future. Many have died fighting to secure and defend our democratic rights and freedoms; exercising our right to vote demonstrates a continued respect for their sacrifice."_

_**11:35 p.m.:**_ Mathematically, only Sima Acan and Tim Crowder in Oakville West and Anita Anand and Ron Chhinzer could win either riding tonight and be elected as MP for the respective seats.

Neither riding has yet been called by Oakville News or any news outlet, and as of 11:30 p.m., none of the candidates have yet arrived at their respective election night events.

_**11:30 p.m.:**_ Two hours after voting closed, about two-thirds of Oakville polls are now reporting results. Both Liberal candidates are still leading in Oakville.

In Oakville West, with 110/195 polls reporting:

*   **Sima Acan,LIB**- 9,379 votes, 50.07 %
*   **Tim Crowder,CON**- 8,766 votes, 46.80 %

In Oakville East, with 135/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 15,185 votes, 49.25 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 14,324 votes, 46.46 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 910 votes, 2.95 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 196 votes, 0.64 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 181 votes, 0.59 %
*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 37 votes, 0.12 %

_**11:25 p.m.:**_ For the NDPs, Oakville News has reached out to both candidates for comment.

Hailey Ford, NDP candidate for Oakville East, told Oakville News tonight: "Of course we're a bit disappointed our voter share, but we always knew this campaign was about building up for the future."

"After this campaign, I'm not going anywhere.I was born and raised here and I want to do the best for this community that I can. To those who voted for me,thank you. The more votes we get, the bigger the message we send and the greater potential we have to be a contender in the future."

Hailey Ford is projected to come third overall in Oakville East, with approximately 1,400 total votes.Diane Downey has not responded to interview requests tonight.

_**11:15 p.m.:**_ As the race grows wider for Anita Anand in Oakville East (now a two point lead over Ron Chhinzer), the lead is shrinking for Sima Acan in Oakville West; where her lead has shrunk to only four points over Tim Crowder.

_**11:00 p.m.:**_ Neither Oakville race has yet been called. Here are the most recent results, 90 minutes after local polls closed.

In Oakville West, with 48/195 polls reporting:

*   **Tim Crowder,CON**- 3,443 votes, 44.97 %

*   **JD Meaney,PPC**- 40 votes, 0.52 %
*   **Martin Gegus,IND**- 11 votes, 0.14 %

In Oakville East, with 60/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 6,241 votes, 48.78 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 6,004 votes, 46.92 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 366 votes, 2.86 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 84 votes, 0.66 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 83 votes, 0.65 %
*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 17 votes, 0.13 %

_**10:50 p.m.:**_ About 1/4 of all polls in Oakville are now reporting, with 40 closed in Oakville West and 50 closed in Oakville East.

_**10:30 p.m.:**_ One hour after Oakville's polls closed, and we have a much clearer picture of what local results will look like.

Sima Acan (Liberal) is still leading in **Oakville West** with a 32 point lead over Tim Crowder and the Conservatives. 10/195 polls are reporting.

Meanwhile, the votes between Anita Anand (Liberal) and Ron Chhinzer (Conservative) remain extremely close in **Oakville East**, with 8/194 polls reporting. Anita is leading by just one vote, 586-585.

_**10:14 p.m.:**_ Multiple sources, including Village Media, [are projecting the federal Liberal party has won the election](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-liberals-win-federal-election-10584170).

This will mark the Liberal's fourth consecutive win, and Mark Carney will remain Canada's Prime Minister. It's still too early to know whether Carney will lead a majority or minority government.

_**Read more here:**_[**Liberals win 2025 federal election**](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-liberals-win-federal-election-10584170)

Of note, a fourth consecutive win for any federal party in Canadian politics is very rare. The last time this happened was also for the Liberals, when they won four elections and led from 1993-2006 under both Jean Chrétien and Paul Martin.

_**10:11 p.m.:**_ While it's too early to call either Oakville riding, it's immediately clear that the race will be significantly closer in Oakville East tonight, with the first results showing an even tie so far in Oakville East.

_**10:10 p.m.:**_**Oakville East's first results are now in.**With the first of 194 polls reporting, early vote suggests a dead-heat tie between Anita Anand for the Liberals and Ron Chhinzer for the Conservatives.

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 42 votes, 41.18 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 42 votes, 41.18 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 14 votes, 13.73 %
*   **Bruno Sousa,GRN**- 3 votes, 2.94 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 1 vote, 0.98 %

Again, with 193 polling stations still to come with results, it's too close to call.

_**10:05 p.m.:**_**Oakville West's first results are in!** With the first poll closing, here are the early results.

*   **Sima Acan,Liberal-**46 votes, 85.19 %
*   **Tim Crowder,Conservative -**7 votes, 12.96 %

While Sima Acan is ahead, the vote share counted is still much too close to call.

_**10:00 p.m.:**_ Polls in Oakville have now been closed for half an hour. Surprisingly, _still_ no polls have begun reporting any results locally.

Across Halton region, [Wellington-Halton Hills North is the first be reporting results](https://www.haltonhillstoday.ca/2025-canada-votes). Milton and Burlington,however, also have no polls yet reporting.

**_9:45 p.m.:_**So far, no polls in Oakville are reporting any results. This likely means most advance voting was not counted earlier today, and those ballot boxes are only being opened now.

**_9:30 p.m.:_**Polls in Ontario, including in Oakville, are now closed. Hundreds of polling stations across town are now counting ballots and should begin reporting results momentarily.

**_9:10 p.m.:_**Elections Canada's website is back up and fully accessible.

**_8:30 p.m.:_**[Polls across Oakville will close in one hour.](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-provincial-election-news/ontario-votes-2025-how-to-vote-in-oakville-today-10293572)Remember, even if the polls have closed,**if you are in line to vote at any location in town after 9:30 p.m., stay in line.**You will still be allowed to vote so long as you remain in line.

**_8:20 p.m.:_**Elections Canada's website has temporarily gone down, reportedly due to heavy traffic. Elections Canada says,"Our website is having technical difficulties. As a result, some of our online services and tools are currently unavailable. We are aware of the issue and are working hard to fix it.We apologize for any inconvenience."

**_7:00 p.m.:_**The first polls have now closed, with Newfoundland's results coming in first. Local polls in Oakville remain open until 9:30 p.m. local time tonight.

**_6:00 p.m.:_**The first polls will be closing in an hour. Under the federal redistribution, the new target number for any party to win a majority government in Canada is 172 or more seats.

**_3:00 p.m.:_**Halfway through the day, several polling places in Oakville have noted short or non-existent lines to vote so far, with most voters in and out within 2-3 minutes or less.

**_2:00 p.m.:_**Multiple sources are reporting at least 7.3 million Canadians voted early in the election - a record number. This could also be a telling sign of record numbers in total cast ballots Canada-wide.

**_12:00 p.m.:_** 24,000 Ontario students participated in a mock election earlier this week. You can see those results who Oakville's youth would choose to be the next Prime Minister [in our story here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/local-news/mock-election-brings-canadian-democracy-to-life-for-local-high-school-students-10571110).

_**11:00 a.m.:**_ This will be the first federal election with Oakville's two new ridings: [Oakville West and Oakville Eas](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/new-oakville-east-oakville-west-ridings-federal-election-10416737)t. Oakville News' [first wrote about these changes earlier this year](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/new-oakville-east-oakville-west-ridings-federal-election-10416737), outlining the new boundaries following the 2021 census.

_**10:15 a.m.:**_ Several south Oakville polling places reported moderate lines at opening this morning, though the original 15-20 minute lines have now mostly disappated, with the average wait time to vote under 5 minutes.

_**9:30 a.m.:**_ Polls are now open in Oakville West and Oakville East, and polls remain open until 9:30 p.m. tonight. Oakville News' guide on how to vote [can be found online here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/its-canadian-election-day-2025-how-to-vote-in-oakville-today-10563270).

## **_Further news from across the country:_**

Polling hours differ across the country, with the first polls closing in Newfoundland at 8:30 p.m.NDT (7 p.m. EDT) and the last polls closing in the west at 7:00 p.m.PDT (10 p.m. EDT).

About one in four eligible voters cast their ballots before election day.

According to preliminary figures from Elections Canada, 7.3 million people voted in advance polls— a 25 per cent increase from 2021.

Liberal Leader Mark Carney triggered the election on March 22 after serving as prime minister for just over a week. Since then, he has positioned himself as the best person to take on U.S. President Donald Trump and lead the country through an economic crisis.

For instance, at an event in Quebec last week, Carney said the question voters must answer is this: "Who's going to be negotiating with President Trump and who's going to be managing the finances of this country?"

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre has run on a platform of change, asking voters to deny the Liberals four more years in power.

"It comes down to one word, change — change, change, change, change, change," he said in Hamilton last week. "Change so you can afford food and housing. Change that you are safe on your streets. Change so we can bring home our jobs and strength. Change to put Canada first."

[Public polling](https://338canada.com/polls.htm) shows that the Liberals opened up a lead over the Conservatives at the outset of the campaign, which has narrowed in recent days.

Those polls have not been kind to Jagmeet Singh's New Democratic Party, which has been polling in a distant third place. Singh has been urging voters to rally around NDP incumbents and send them back to Ottawa to hold what he expects to be a Liberal government accountable.

The Green Party and its co-leaders,Jonathan Pedneault and Elizabeth May, are hoping to protect the party's incumbents, May in Saanich—Gulf Islands and Mike Morrice in Kitchener Centre, and re-elect former MP Paul Manly in Nanaimo—Ladysmith. The party has also singled out Pedneault's riding of Outremont, as well as Fredericton—Oromocto and Guelph, as electoral targets.

Meanwhile,Bloc Québécois leader Yves-François Blanchet recently made headlines for riling up his sovereigntist base for calling[Canada "an artificial country with very little meaning."](https://www.ctvnews.ca/federal-election-2025/article/blanchet-calls-canada-an-artificial-country-with-very-little-meaning/)

You can follow the results of the election as they come in here, and on [our Canada Votes home page](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-canada-votes).

The local results of Canada's 2025 federal election are almost complete. Both Sima Acan and Anita Anand for the Liberals have been elected as MPs for Oakville West and Oakville East respectively.

In total, a record-breaking number of Canadians cast their vote. More than 18.2 million balltos were cast in this election.

This website will be updating live tonight as results are reported by the polling stations.

For the latest developments in the national race, go to our[Canada Votes page](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-canada-votes).

Live results from the new Oakville West and East ridings will available on this website all night long just below in this story. Up-to-the-minute updates from Oakville and across Canada are available below those graphs.

Polls are now closed in Oakville, and results are available here:

## _Live updates across Oakville:_

**_3:00 a.m.:_**This concludes Oakville News' live coverage of Canada's Election Night 2025. This story and its links will remain on the website indefinitely. Good night!

_**2:45 a.m.:**_ No additional polls have submitted results in the last hour, and final results aren't expected until at least tomorrow.

_**2:30 a.m.:**_ Around Halton, Liberal candidates have won in Burlington and Burlington North-Milton West, while Conservatives won in Wellington-Halton Hills. The new Milton East-Halton Hills South riding is still too close to call, though Conservative Parm Gill has a 0.2 per cent lead as of press time.

_**2:15 a.m.:**_ Oakville News has spoken with campaign officials for Tim Crowder and Ron Chhinzer, and neither have responded to our requests for comment. There has also been no comment from Alicia Bedford, who ran for the United Party in Oakville East.

_**2:00 a.m.:**_ Almost all polls are now reporting in Oakville, and the results are nearly final. Only one poll in Oakville West and five polls in Oakville East have yet to send in their results.

In Oakville West, with 194/195 polls reporting:

_**1:35 a.m.:**_ Newly elected Prime Minister Mark Carney, addressing Canadians at his acceptance speech, says "When Canada seeks unity and kindness, Canada grows."

_**1:15 a.m.:**_ Re-elected MP Anita Anand, on her win tonight, told Oakville News that, "It's about making sure that we're able to stand out for the values that make Canada strong."

_**1:10 a.m.:**_ On her win tonight, newly elected Oakville West MP Sima Acan told Oakville News: "This is life changing. It's a step that I am taking now for public service which was always in me."

_**11:25 p.m.:**_ For the NDPs, Oakville News has reached out to both candidates for comment.

Hailey Ford, NDP candidate for Oakville East, told Oakville News tonight: "Of course we're a bit disappointed our voter share, but we always knew this campaign was about building up for the future."

"After this campaign, I'm not going anywhere.I was born and raised here and I want to do the best for this community that I can. To those who voted for me,thank you. The more votes we get, the bigger the message we send and the greater potential we have to be a contender in the future."

Hailey Ford is projected to come third overall in Oakville East, with approximately 1,400 total votes.Diane Downey has not responded to interview requests tonight.

_**11:15 p.m.:**_ As the race grows wider for Anita Anand in Oakville East (now a two point lead over Ron Chhinzer), the lead is shrinking for Sima Acan in Oakville West; where her lead has shrunk to only four points over Tim Crowder.

_**11:00 p.m.:**_ Neither Oakville race has yet been called. Here are the most recent results, 90 minutes after local polls closed.

*   **JD Meaney,PPC**- 40 votes, 0.52 %
*   **Martin Gegus,IND**- 11 votes, 0.14 %

In Oakville East, with 60/194 polls reporting:

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 6,241 votes, 48.78 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 6,004 votes, 46.92 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 366 votes, 2.86 %
*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 84 votes, 0.66 %

*   **Alicia Bedford,UPC**- 17 votes, 0.13 %

_**10:50 p.m.:**_ About 1/4 of all polls in Oakville are now reporting, with 40 closed in Oakville West and 50 closed in Oakville East.

_**10:30 p.m.:**_ One hour after Oakville's polls closed, and we have a much clearer picture of what local results will look like.

Sima Acan (Liberal) is still leading in **Oakville West** with a 32 point lead over Tim Crowder and the Conservatives. 10/195 polls are reporting.

Meanwhile, the votes between Anita Anand (Liberal) and Ron Chhinzer (Conservative) remain extremely close in **Oakville East**, with 8/194 polls reporting. Anita is leading by just one vote, 586-585.

_**10:14 p.m.:**_ Multiple sources, including Village Media, [are projecting the federal Liberal party has won the election](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-liberals-win-federal-election-10584170).

This will mark the Liberal's fourth consecutive win, and Mark Carney will remain Canada's Prime Minister. It's still too early to know whether Carney will lead a majority or minority government.

_**Read more here:**_[**Liberals win 2025 federal election**](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/breaking-liberals-win-federal-election-10584170)

Of note, a fourth consecutive win for any federal party in Canadian politics is very rare. The last time this happened was also for the Liberals, when they won four elections and led from 1993-2006 under both Jean Chrétien and Paul Martin.

_**10:11 p.m.:**_ While it's too early to call either Oakville riding, it's immediately clear that the race will be significantly closer in Oakville East tonight, with the first results showing an even tie so far in Oakville East.

_**10:10 p.m.:**_**Oakville East's first results are now in.**With the first of 194 polls reporting, early vote suggests a dead-heat tie between Anita Anand for the Liberals and Ron Chhinzer for the Conservatives.

*   **Anita Anand,LIB**- 42 votes, 41.18 %
*   **Ron Chhinzer,CON**- 42 votes, 41.18 %
*   **Hailey Ford,NDP**- 14 votes, 13.73 %

*   **Henry Karabela,PPC**- 1 vote, 0.98 %

Again, with 193 polling stations still to come with results, it's too close to call.

_**10:00 p.m.:**_ Polls in Oakville have now been closed for half an hour. Surprisingly, _still_ no polls have begun reporting any results locally.

Across Halton region, [Wellington-Halton Hills North is the first be reporting results](https://www.haltonhillstoday.ca/2025-canada-votes). Milton and Burlington,however, also have no polls yet reporting.

**_9:45 p.m.:_**So far, no polls in Oakville are reporting any results. This likely means most advance voting was not counted earlier today, and those ballot boxes are only being opened now.

**_9:30 p.m.:_**Polls in Ontario, including in Oakville, are now closed. Hundreds of polling stations across town are now counting ballots and should begin reporting results momentarily.

**_9:10 p.m.:_**Elections Canada's website is back up and fully accessible.

**_8:30 p.m.:_**[Polls across Oakville will close in one hour.](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-provincial-election-news/ontario-votes-2025-how-to-vote-in-oakville-today-10293572)Remember, even if the polls have closed,**if you are in line to vote at any location in town after 9:30 p.m., stay in line.**You will still be allowed to vote so long as you remain in line.

**_8:20 p.m.:_**Elections Canada's website has temporarily gone down, reportedly due to heavy traffic. Elections Canada says,"Our website is having technical difficulties. As a result, some of our online services and tools are currently unavailable. We are aware of the issue and are working hard to fix it.We apologize for any inconvenience."

**_6:00 p.m.:_**The first polls will be closing in an hour. Under the federal redistribution, the new target number for any party to win a majority government in Canada is 172 or more seats.

**_3:00 p.m.:_**Halfway through the day, several polling places in Oakville have noted short or non-existent lines to vote so far, with most voters in and out within 2-3 minutes or less.

**_2:00 p.m.:_**Multiple sources are reporting at least 7.3 million Canadians voted early in the election - a record number. This could also be a telling sign of record numbers in total cast ballots Canada-wide.

**_12:00 p.m.:_** 24,000 Ontario students participated in a mock election earlier this week. You can see those results who Oakville's youth would choose to be the next Prime Minister [in our story here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/local-news/mock-election-brings-canadian-democracy-to-life-for-local-high-school-students-10571110).

_**11:00 a.m.:**_ This will be the first federal election with Oakville's two new ridings: [Oakville West and Oakville Eas](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/new-oakville-east-oakville-west-ridings-federal-election-10416737)t. Oakville News' [first wrote about these changes earlier this year](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/new-oakville-east-oakville-west-ridings-federal-election-10416737), outlining the new boundaries following the 2021 census.

_**10:15 a.m.:**_ Several south Oakville polling places reported moderate lines at opening this morning, though the original 15-20 minute lines have now mostly disappated, with the average wait time to vote under 5 minutes.

_**9:30 a.m.:**_ Polls are now open in Oakville West and Oakville East, and polls remain open until 9:30 p.m. tonight. Oakville News' guide on how to vote [can be found online here](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-federal-election-news/its-canadian-election-day-2025-how-to-vote-in-oakville-today-10563270).

## **_Further news from across the country:_**

Polling hours differ across the country, with the first polls closing in Newfoundland at 8:30 p.m.NDT (7 p.m. EDT) and the last polls closing in the west at 7:00 p.m.PDT (10 p.m. EDT).

About one in four eligible voters cast their ballots before election day.

According to preliminary figures from Elections Canada, 7.3 million people voted in advance polls— a 25 per cent increase from 2021.

Liberal Leader Mark Carney triggered the election on March 22 after serving as prime minister for just over a week. Since then, he has positioned himself as the best person to take on U.S. President Donald Trump and lead the country through an economic crisis.

For instance, at an event in Quebec last week, Carney said the question voters must answer is this: "Who's going to be negotiating with President Trump and who's going to be managing the finances of this country?"

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre has run on a platform of change, asking voters to deny the Liberals four more years in power.

"It comes down to one word, change — change, change, change, change, change," he said in Hamilton last week. "Change so you can afford food and housing. Change that you are safe on your streets. Change so we can bring home our jobs and strength. Change to put Canada first."

[Public polling](https://338canada.com/polls.htm) shows that the Liberals opened up a lead over the Conservatives at the outset of the campaign, which has narrowed in recent days.

Those polls have not been kind to Jagmeet Singh's New Democratic Party, which has been polling in a distant third place. Singh has been urging voters to rally around NDP incumbents and send them back to Ottawa to hold what he expects to be a Liberal government accountable.

The Green Party and its co-leaders,Jonathan Pedneault and Elizabeth May, are hoping to protect the party's incumbents, May in Saanich—Gulf Islands and Mike Morrice in Kitchener Centre, and re-elect former MP Paul Manly in Nanaimo—Ladysmith. The party has also singled out Pedneault's riding of Outremont, as well as Fredericton—Oromocto and Guelph, as electoral targets.

Meanwhile,Bloc Québécois leader Yves-François Blanchet recently made headlines for riling up his sovereigntist base for calling[Canada "an artificial country with very little meaning."](https://www.ctvnews.ca/federal-election-2025/article/blanchet-calls-canada-an-artificial-country-with-very-little-meaning/)

You can follow the results of the election as they come in here, and on [our Canada Votes home page](https://www.oakvillenews.org/2025-canada-votes).

# Appendix 12: General Election Results Since 1867

Members are elected to the House of Commons under different political affiliations. A majority government is formed when the same political party holds the majority of seats or when the majority of members share a similar political affiliation. Most governments since 1867 have been majority governments. However, the general elections of 1921, 1925, 1957, 1962, 1963, 1965, 1972, 1979, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2019, 2021 and 2025 resulted in minority governments.

## Footnotes

1.   1
The numbers reflect the results immediately following the general election and do not take into account changes in political affiliation, resignations, deaths or elections subsequently declared null and void.

2.   2
The results were obtained by accounting for the political affiliation of the member of Parliament elected in each of the electoral districts in the general election.

3.   3
In the general elections of 1867 and 1872, elections in the constituencies were held at various times between the dates listed. After 1874 and the Dominion Elections Act, the holding of the general election on the same day became mandatory, with certain exceptions because of physical difficulties in some areas.

4.   4
Due to riots, the returning officer made a special report and there was no election in Kamouraska, Quebec. A by-election was held on February 17, 1869.

5.   5
Liberal-Conservative and Conservative members always sat together in the House of Commons and, if applicable, in the same government.

6.   6
On November 5, 1873, the government led by Liberal-Conservative Sir John A. Macdonald resigned as a result of the Canadian Pacific Railway scandal. On November 7, 1873, the Liberals, led by Alexander Mackenzie, formed a government and the second session was prorogued. The Second Parliament was subsequently dissolved on January 2, 1874.

7.   7
During the First World War, the term of the 12th Parliament was extended beyond five years. On February 8, 1916, the House adopted an Address to His Majesty the King requesting that the term of that Parliament be extended to October 7, 1917 (Journals, [p. 62](https://parl.canadiana.ca/view/oop.HOC_1206_52_01/72)).

8.   8
On October 12, 1917, Prime Minister Sir Robert Borden formed a cabinet known as the Unionist government, which brought together Conservative, Liberal-Conservative and Liberal members of Parliament who supported conscription during the First World War. These members campaigned under the Unionist banner and were elected in the general election of December 17, 1917. The results of the 1917 general election led to a majority Unionist government.

9.   9
Following the reorganization of political affiliations resulting from the conscription issue in 1917, the Liberals who did not join the Unionists and who remained loyal to Sir Wilfrid Laurier were called Laurier Liberals.

10.   10
Although the Liberals elected 118 members, the minimum number required to have a majority of seats in the House, in the general election of December 6, 1921, changes in political affiliation, resignations, by-elections and deaths in office caused the Liberals to swing between a majority and minority of seats. The government formed by W. L. Mackenzie King was therefore considered the first minority government since 1867. The Liberals were able to govern with the support of the Progressives.

11.   11
Even though the Conservatives elected more members than the Liberals, Liberal leader W. L. Mackenzie King, himself defeated in York North, Ontario, remained Prime Minister with the support of the Progressives. Mr. King was elected in a by-election on February 15, 1926, and returned to the House on March 15, 1926. On June 26, 1926, the Prime Minister asked the Governor General to dissolve Parliament and order a general election. The Governor General refused and W. L. Mackenzie King resigned. The Governor General subsequently asked Conservative member Arthur Meighen to form a government, which he did on June 29, 1926. His minority government lost the confidence of the House two days later, on July 1, 1926. The 15th Parliament was dissolved the following day.

12.   12
Even though the Liberals elected a minority of members with 116, W. L. Mackenzie King was able to form a government regarded as a majority due to the support of Liberal Progressive members.

13.   13
In the 1940 general election, the Conservative Party and its leader, Robert James Manion, campaigned under the National Government banner while some Conservative candidates campaigned under the traditional banner.

14.   14
Like in 1926, even though the Liberals elected a minority of members with 118, they were able to form a majority government with the support of Independent Liberal members and a Liberal Progressive member.

15.   15
The Conservative Party became the Progressive Conservative Party on December 11, 1942. Previously, in the 19th Parliament, Progressive Conservative candidates were elected in by-elections.

16.   16
In 1955, the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation changed its name in French to the Parti social démocratique du Canada. The party name, Co-operative Commonwealth Federation, remained unchanged in English.

17.   17
In 1961, the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation was dissolved and became the New Democratic Party.

18.   18
On September 1, 1963, 13 members forming the Quebec wing of the Social Credit Party of Canada left the party to form the Ralliement des créditistes under the leadership of Réal Caouette. Candidates were subsequently elected under the banner of the Ralliement des créditistes in the general election of November 8, 1965.

19.   19
In 1967, Ralliement des créditistes changed its name to Ralliement créditiste.

20.   20
In 1971, Ralliement créditiste members returned to the Social Credit Party of Canada and Réal Caouette became the leader of the party. He subsequently led the party’s campaign and was re-elected in the electoral district of Témiscamingue in the general election of October 30, 1972.

21.   21
In 2000, the Reform Party was dissolved and became the Canadian Reform Conservative Alliance.

22.   22
In 2003, the Progressive Conservative Party merged with the Canadian Reform Conservative Alliance to become the Conservative Party of Canada.

23.   23
Although the Liberals elected a minority of members with 160, they were able to govern with the support of the New Democratic Party. Under a supply and confidence agreement concluded between the two parties in March 2022, the New Democratic Party committed to supporting the government on confidence and budgetary matters in exchange for progress on certain policies. This agreement ended in September 2024.

# Appendix 12: General Election Results Since 1867

Members are elected to the House of Commons under different political affiliations. A majority government is formed when the same political party holds the majority of seats or when the majority of members share a similar political affiliation. Most governments since 1867 have been majority governments. However, the general elections of 1921, 1925, 1957, 1962, 1963, 1965, 1972, 1979, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2019, 2021 and 2025 resulted in minority governments.

## Footnotes

1.   1
The numbers reflect the results immediately following the general election and do not take into account changes in political affiliation, resignations, deaths or elections subsequently declared null and void.

2.   2
The results were obtained by accounting for the political affiliation of the member of Parliament elected in each of the electoral districts in the general election.

3.   3
In the general elections of 1867 and 1872, elections in the constituencies were held at various times between the dates listed. After 1874 and the Dominion Elections Act, the holding of the general election on the same day became mandatory, with certain exceptions because of physical difficulties in some areas.

4.   4
Due to riots, the returning officer made a special report and there was no election in Kamouraska, Quebec. A by-election was held on February 17, 1869.

5.   5
Liberal-Conservative and Conservative members always sat together in the House of Commons and, if applicable, in the same government.

6.   6
On November 5, 1873, the government led by Liberal-Conservative Sir John A. Macdonald resigned as a result of the Canadian Pacific Railway scandal. On November 7, 1873, the Liberals, led by Alexander Mackenzie, formed a government and the second session was prorogued. The Second Parliament was subsequently dissolved on January 2, 1874.

7.   7
During the First World War, the term of the 12th Parliament was extended beyond five years. On February 8, 1916, the House adopted an Address to His Majesty the King requesting that the term of that Parliament be extended to October 7, 1917 (Journals, [p. 62](https://parl.canadiana.ca/view/oop.HOC_1206_52_01/72)).

8.   8
On October 12, 1917, Prime Minister Sir Robert Borden formed a cabinet known as the Unionist government, which brought together Conservative, Liberal-Conservative and Liberal members of Parliament who supported conscription during the First World War. These members campaigned under the Unionist banner and were elected in the general election of December 17, 1917. The results of the 1917 general election led to a majority Unionist government.

9.   9
Following the reorganization of political affiliations resulting from the conscription issue in 1917, the Liberals who did not join the Unionists and who remained loyal to Sir Wilfrid Laurier were called Laurier Liberals.

10.   10
Although the Liberals elected 118 members, the minimum number required to have a majority of seats in the House, in the general election of December 6, 1921, changes in political affiliation, resignations, by-elections and deaths in office caused the Liberals to swing between a majority and minority of seats. The government formed by W. L. Mackenzie King was therefore considered the first minority government since 1867. The Liberals were able to govern with the support of the Progressives.

11.   11
Even though the Conservatives elected more members than the Liberals, Liberal leader W. L. Mackenzie King, himself defeated in York North, Ontario, remained Prime Minister with the support of the Progressives. Mr. King was elected in a by-election on February 15, 1926, and returned to the House on March 15, 1926. On June 26, 1926, the Prime Minister asked the Governor General to dissolve Parliament and order a general election. The Governor General refused and W. L. Mackenzie King resigned. The Governor General subsequently asked Conservative member Arthur Meighen to form a government, which he did on June 29, 1926. His minority government lost the confidence of the House two days later, on July 1, 1926. The 15th Parliament was dissolved the following day.

12.   12
Even though the Liberals elected a minority of members with 116, W. L. Mackenzie King was able to form a government regarded as a majority due to the support of Liberal Progressive members.

13.   13
In the 1940 general election, the Conservative Party and its leader, Robert James Manion, campaigned under the National Government banner while some Conservative candidates campaigned under the traditional banner.

14.   14
Like in 1926, even though the Liberals elected a minority of members with 118, they were able to form a majority government with the support of Independent Liberal members and a Liberal Progressive member.

15.   15
The Conservative Party became the Progressive Conservative Party on December 11, 1942. Previously, in the 19th Parliament, Progressive Conservative candidates were elected in by-elections.

16.   16
In 1955, the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation changed its name in French to the Parti social démocratique du Canada. The party name, Co-operative Commonwealth Federation, remained unchanged in English.

17.   17
In 1961, the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation was dissolved and became the New Democratic Party.

18.   18
On September 1, 1963, 13 members forming the Quebec wing of the Social Credit Party of Canada left the party to form the Ralliement des créditistes under the leadership of Réal Caouette. Candidates were subsequently elected under the banner of the Ralliement des créditistes in the general election of November 8, 1965.

19.   19
In 1967, Ralliement des créditistes changed its name to Ralliement créditiste.

20.   20
In 1971, Ralliement créditiste members returned to the Social Credit Party of Canada and Réal Caouette became the leader of the party. He subsequently led the party’s campaign and was re-elected in the electoral district of Témiscamingue in the general election of October 30, 1972.

21.   21
In 2000, the Reform Party was dissolved and became the Canadian Reform Conservative Alliance.

22.   22
In 2003, the Progressive Conservative Party merged with the Canadian Reform Conservative Alliance to become the Conservative Party of Canada.

23.   23
Although the Liberals elected a minority of members with 160, they were able to govern with the support of the New Democratic Party. Under a supply and confidence agreement concluded between the two parties in March 2022, the New Democratic Party committed to supporting the government on confidence and budgetary matters in exchange for progress on certain policies. This agreement ended in September 2024.
